title: The Case Study Method's Roots in 1870s Harvard Law School
explainer: The case-study format did not start in business or tech - it was pioneered around 1870 by Christopher Columbus Langdell at Harvard Law School, who had students analyze real court decisions instead of memorizing abstract legal rules. Harvard Business School adapted the same approach starting in the 1920s, swapping case law for real business dilemmas narrated from a decision-maker's point of view. The structure expected of a portfolio case study - frame the problem, give context, walk through the decision, show the outcome - descends directly from that century-old teaching method, which is why it reads as a specific genre rather than just 'a write-up.'
